head: 02fe393c18a24d617819a97d3e22d3a1a8d91726
title: Compute tie-aware ADR target ranks without quadratic comparison tensors
body:
## Change

Compute ADRMSELoss's target ranks with a row sort and two searchsorted bounds instead of constructing two batch-by-document-by-document comparison tensors. The bounds preserve the existing average-rank treatment of ties, padded documents, infinities and NaN labels. Target preparation becomes O(B N log N); the differentiable predicted-rank calculation remains quadratic.

This changes the current tie-aware target path. Earlier double-argsort implementations assigned arbitrary ranks to equal labels and are not reused.

## Validation and benchmark

[Exact-base validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43925134003) compares base `9ac7fdb4` with candidate `02fe393c` on CPU with PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. All **121 new compatibility tests pass on both revisions**. Candidate tests together with the existing CrossEncoder loss tests produce **233 passes and 6 skips** in each environment. All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The tests compare the public loss and score gradients against an independent per-query Python rank calculation and float64 sigmoid objective. They cover ties, negative labels, padding, infinities, NaNs, four label dtypes, three alpha values, and different minibatch sizes.

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/71ca95fd68df8c3fe2964e57462829611e764a29/.validation/st-adr-ranks-benchmark.py) runs the public loss forward and backward for four ragged queries using a deterministic score-table CrossEncoder. It includes target preparation and predicted-rank work, with two warmups and five timed repetitions. Transformer inference is outside the measured workload.

| PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU query lengths | Before median | After median | Ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128, 64, 127, 32 | 0.690 ms | 0.638 ms | 1.08× |
| 512, 256, 511, 128 | 9.836 ms | 9.683 ms | 1.02× |
| 2,048, 1,024, 2,047, 512 | 397.69 ms | 239.89 ms | 1.66× |

The independent PyTorch 2.6.0 runner measured 1.08×, 1.27× and 1.68×, respectively. Losses and gradient SHA-256 digests match exactly in every benchmark case. The benefit grows with the document count; these measurements do not claim a whole-model training speedup.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation, compatibility tests and benchmarking.
